item.text:
**8B.5 Research Note: Ali Khamenei in 2024**

**Bottom line**
- **Weak yes, but uneven.** Khamenei’s system showed real cross-institutional control in the coercive, electoral, and sanctions-avoidance spheres.
- The weakest point was not political control but **administrative follow-through in civilian domains**: water, inspections, and broader service delivery show coordination gaps and noncompliance.

- **Iran’s presidential election dominated by Khamenei loyalists** | Reuters | 2024-06-25 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/irans-presidential-election-dominated-by-khamenei-loyalists-3494879 | Claim: Reuters said Khamenei ensured hardline candidates dominated the contest and the Guardian Council approved only five hardliners and one low-profile moderate from 80 applicants. This is strong evidence of regime-wide control over candidate selection and elite coordination. | IDs: `8B.5`, `8B.2`, `7B.9`

- **Pezeshkian Cabinet Profiles** | The Iran Primer / USIP | 2024-08-22 | https://iranprimer.usip.org/index.php/blog/2024/aug/22/pezeshkian-cabinet-profiles | Claim: The cabinet included reformists, hardliners, technocrats, and academics, and the list reportedly had Khamenei, IRGC, and security-agency approval before submission. That suggests Khamenei’s camp still controlled staffing and could coordinate across the ruling network, even if the result was compromise-driven. | IDs: `8B.5`, `8B.4`, `8B.2`

- **Iran: New compulsory veiling law intensifies oppression of women and girls** | Amnesty International | 2024-12-10 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/12/iran-new-compulsory-veiling-law-intensifies-oppression-of-women-and-girls/ | Claim: Amnesty says the judiciary drafted the law, the Guardian Council approved it, parliament set it in motion, and enforcement powers expanded for police, intelligence, IRGC, and Basij. This is clear evidence of coordinated follow-through across institutions for a coercive internal program. | IDs: `8B.5`, `8B.4`, `8B.2`, `7B.7`

- **Iran: Draconian campaign to enforce compulsory veiling laws through surveillance and mass car confiscations** | Amnesty International | 2024-03-06 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/03/iran-draconian-campaign-to-enforce-compulsory-veiling-laws-through-surveillance-and-mass-car-confiscations/ | Claim: Amnesty reported a multi-agency campaign involving police, courts, prosecutors, intelligence, IRGC, and Basij, with surveillance, confiscations, prosecutions, flogging, and morality classes. This is strong evidence that Khamenei’s system could mobilize implementing agencies in a disciplined way for repression. | IDs: `8B.5`, `8B.4`, `8B.2`, `7B.7`

- **Iran’s Revolutionary Guards extend control over Tehran’s oil exports, sources say** | Reuters / Investing.com | 2024-12-18 | https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/irans-revolutionary-guards-extend-control-over-tehrans-oil-exports-sources-say-3778558 | Claim: Reuters reported the IRGC controlled up to half of Iran’s oil exports through shadow fleets and front companies. That shows strong control and follow-through in a core revenue and sanctions-evasion channel, with security networks coordinating commercial logistics. | IDs: `8B.5`, `8B.4`, `8B.2`, `7B.9`

- **Iran will not impede IAEA access, head of its atomic organisation says** | Reuters | 2024-12-14 | https://theprint.in/world/iran-will-not-impede-iaea-access-head-of-its-atomic-organisation-says/2403254/ | Claim: Iran said it would not obstruct UN watchdog access and would work within safeguards. This is a narrow positive signal that the regime could still coordinate a procedural compliance posture in the nuclear file. | IDs: `8B.5`, `8B.2`, `8B.1`

- **IAEA board passes resolution against Iran on cooperation, inspectors** | Reuters | 2024-06-05 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/iaea-board-passes-resolution-against-iran-on-cooperation-inspectors-3472087 | Claim: Reuters said Iran barred many experienced inspectors and the IAEA Board demanded reversal. This is strong negative evidence on disciplined follow-through in a sensitive domain, showing that bureaucratic coordination could break down when it conflicted with regime control. | IDs: `8B.5`, `8B.2`, `8B.1`

- **Iran’s water crisis leads to alarming ground collapse** | DW | 2024-06-19 | https://amp.dw.com/en/irans-water-crisis-leads-to-alarming-ground-collapse/a-69405927 | Claim: DW reported drought and water shortages causing land subsidence, threatening Tehran and hundreds of other towns and affecting at least half of Iranian society. This is negative evidence on civilian follow-through across ministries and regions: the state was not effectively coordinating a major service crisis. | IDs: `8B.5`, `8B.2`

- **Journalists ordered to serve five years in prison in Iran** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-10-24 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/10/24/journalists-ordered-serve-five-years-prison-iran | Claim: HRW said the judiciary enforced prison terms against journalists for reporting on Mahsa Amini’s death. That shows the coercive apparatus remained coordinated, but in a punitive way rather than as evidence of accountable administrative discipline. | IDs: `8B.5`, `7B.7`, `7B.10`

**Search gap**
- I found **no 2024 source showing a formal cross-ministry discipline system**, internal performance dashboard, or explicit enforcement chain for non-security policy execution.
- The strongest evidence is **sector-specific**: elite vetting, repression, oil-export control, and partial nuclear procedural compliance. The civilian/service side remains weakly evidenced and includes clear failures.
